    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }

       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */

    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */

      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="265.8mm" height="33.99mm" viewBox="0 6.01 265.8 33.99">
  <!-- nvidia/rtx-4500-ada: THE SHROUD'S LOWER EDGE, the body's left side seen from
       outside. Across: 266.7 less mm behind the bracket's outer face, so the
       card's far end is at the left and the bracket's end at 265.8. Down: the
       face's y, the shroud's 6.01 to 40.0. A plain dark edge: no photograph
       shows it, and the broad side's photograph shows it flat. -->
  <rect x="0" y="6.01" width="265.8" height="33.99" fill="#232325"/>
</svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="265.8mm" height="38.23mm" viewBox="0.9 1.77 265.8 38.23">
  <!-- nvidia/rtx-4500-ada: THE TOP EDGE, the body's right side seen from outside.
       Across: mm behind the bracket's outer face (0.9 to 266.7, the shroud's
       length). Down: the face's y (1.77 the backplate's outer face, 4.44 the
       board's outer face, 40.0 the shroud's). Every piece whose right side is the card's top edge `shows:
       [right]` and carries its patch of this. The champagne strip is the heat
       sink's fins showing on the edge, with its bay where the blower's ring comes
       near; its place is estimated from NVIDIA's render of the RTX 5000 Ada, which
       shows the same family's edge (provenance body-top-edge). The maker's mark is
       reserved, not drawn. -->
  <defs>
    <pattern id="fins" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse" x="0.9" y="14" width="1.2" height="20">
      <rect x="0" y="0" width="1.2" height="20" fill="#c8b283"/>
      <rect x="0.8" y="0" width="0.4" height="20" fill="#8d7a56"/>
    </pattern>
  </defs>
  <!-- the backplate's edge, the board's edge and the black shroud -->
  <rect x="0.9" y="1.77" width="265.8" height="2.67" fill="#202326"/>
  <rect x="0.9" y="4.44" width="265.8" height="1.57" fill="#1d2420"/>
  <rect x="0.9" y="6.01" width="265.8" height="33.99" fill="#18181a"/>
  <!-- the fin strip, with its bay at the blower -->
  <path id="fin-strip" d="M46 14 L158 14 C165 14 167 25 176 25 L218 25 C227 25 229 14 236 14 L250 14 L250 34 L46 34 Z" fill="url(#fins)"/>
  <!-- the mark is reserved, not drawn (L172) -->
  <rect id="logo-zone" x="232.0" y="7.6" width="22.0" height="4.6" fill="none"/>
  <g id="silkscreen">
    <text x="6.0" y="11.0" font-family="Arial" font-weight="bold" font-size="2.4" fill="#bdb8aa">RTX 4500</text>
  </g>
</svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="97.9mm" height="265.8mm" viewBox="28.41 0 97.9 265.8">
  <!-- nvidia/rtx-4500-ada: THE BACKPLATE, the body's top side seen from outside
       (from the board's rear). Across: the face's x, the lower edge at 28.41 and
       the top edge at 126.31. Down: 266.7 less mm behind the bracket's outer face,
       so the far end is at the top and the bracket's end at the bottom. A matte
       black plate with ten small screws (PNY's back photograph at 2.61 px/mm,
       provenance body-backplate). Drawn in-house; nothing is traced. -->
  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="plate-shade" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
      <stop offset="0" stop-color="#2d2d2f"/>
      <stop offset="1" stop-color="#1b1b1d"/>
    </linearGradient>
  </defs>
  <rect x="28.41" y="0" width="97.9" height="265.8" fill="url(#plate-shade)"/>
  <g id="backplate-screws" fill="#0c0c0d" stroke="#3f3f42" stroke-width="0.3">
    <circle cx="122.9" cy="260.6" r="1.7"/>
    <circle cx="122.9" cy="174.9" r="1.7"/>
    <circle cx="122.9" cy="97.2" r="1.7"/>
    <circle cx="122.9" cy="18.7" r="1.7"/>
    <circle cx="32.2" cy="250.2" r="1.7"/>
    <circle cx="32.2" cy="174.9" r="1.7"/>
    <circle cx="32.2" cy="97.2" r="1.7"/>
    <circle cx="32.2" cy="18.7" r="1.7"/>
    <circle cx="100.0" cy="4.1" r="1.7"/>
    <circle cx="55.1" cy="4.1" r="1.7"/>
  </g>
</svg>

</svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="265.8mm" height="38.23mm" viewBox="0.9 1.77 265.8 38.23">
  <!-- nvidia/rtx-5000-ada: THE TOP EDGE, the body's right side seen from outside.
       Across: mm behind the bracket's outer face (0.9 to 266.7, the shroud's
       length). Down: the face's y (1.77 the backplate's outer face, 4.44 the
       board's outer face, 40.0 the shroud's). Every piece whose right side is the
       card's top edge `shows: [right]` and carries its patch of this. The champagne
       strip is the heat sink's fins showing on the edge, with its bay where the
       blower's ring comes near; its place is estimated from NVIDIA's own render of
       this card, which shows the edge in a 3/4 view that cannot be scaled
       (provenance body-top-edge). The maker's mark is reserved, not drawn. -->

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="97.9mm" height="265.8mm" viewBox="28.41 0 97.9 265.8">

       (from the board's rear). NO PHOTOGRAPH OF THIS CARD'S BACK IS HELD (PNY serves

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="265.8mm" height="35.56mm" viewBox="0.9 4.44 265.8 35.56">
  <!-- nvidia/rtx-6000-ada: THE TOP EDGE, the body's right side seen from outside.
       Across: mm behind the bracket's outer face (0.9 to 266.7, the shroud's
       length). Down: the face's y (4.44 the board's outer face, 40.0 the
       shroud's). Every piece whose right side is the card's top edge `shows:
       [right]` and carries its patch of this. The champagne strip is the heat
       sink's fins showing on the edge, with its bay where the blower's ring comes

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="120.02mm" height="41.91mm" viewBox="0 0 120.02 41.91">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="97.9mm" height="35.56mm" viewBox="0 0 97.9 35.56">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="161.66mm" height="16.04mm" viewBox="0.9 1.27 161.66 16.04">

       Across: mm behind the bracket's outer face (0.9 to 162.56). Down: the face's
       y (1.27 the board's outer face, 17.31 the shroud's). Every piece whose right
       side is the card's top edge `shows: [right]` and carries its patch of this.
       The shroud's top is a grey frame around a long flat lid that runs from the
       shroud's near end nearly to the far end, darker at the near end and lighter
       toward the blower, as PNY's 3/4 view lights it, with a black pocket past the
       lid's rounded end. There is no champagne heat-sink strip on this card. The
       lid's places are fractions read off a 3/4 view and are estimated (provenance
       body-top-edge). -->

    <linearGradient id="lid" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
      <stop offset="0" stop-color="#222223"/>
      <stop offset="0.6" stop-color="#4d4d50"/>

  <rect x="0.9" y="2.84" width="161.66" height="14.47" fill="#4a4a4d"/>

       Across: mm behind the bracket's outer face (0.9 to 167.64, the shroud's
       length). Down: the face's y (4.44 the board's outer face, 40.0 the
       shroud's). Every piece whose right side is the card's top edge `shows:
       [right]` and carries its patch of this. The top edge is a grey frame around
       a long flat lid that runs from the bracket end nearly to the far end,
       darker at the bracket end and lighter toward the blower, as PNY's 3/4 view
       lights it, with a black pocket past the lid's rounded end. There is no
       champagne heat-sink strip on this card. The lid's places are fractions
       read off a 3/4 view and are estimated (provenance body-top-edge). -->
  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="lid" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
      <stop offset="0" stop-color="#222223"/>
      <stop offset="0.6" stop-color="#4d4d50"/>
      <stop offset="1" stop-color="#6a6a6e"/>

  </g>
</svg>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="79.2mm" height="18.42mm" viewBox="0 0 79.2 18.42">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="97.9mm" height="35.56mm" viewBox="0 0 97.9 35.56">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="265.8mm" height="35.56mm" viewBox="0.9 4.44 265.8 35.56">
  <!-- nvidia/rtx-a5500: THE TOP EDGE, the body's right side seen from outside.
       Across: mm behind the bracket's outer face (0.9 to 266.7, the shroud's
       length). Down: the face's y (4.44 the board's outer face, 40.0 the
       shroud's). Every piece whose right side is the card's top edge `shows:
       [right]` and carries its patch of this. The top edge is a frame, grey as
       PNY's 3/4 view lights it, around a slot that runs nearly the whole length;
       the heat sink's champagne top fills the slot from 11.5 to 252.5 behind the
       bracket, with a bay cut into its board side around the blower (163 to 205)
       and a rounded end, and the slot is black beyond it. Its places are fractions
       read off a 3/4 view and are estimated (provenance body-top-edge). The
       NVLink, stereo and sync connectors the same view shows are not drawn. -->
  <!-- the board's edge and the frame's top -->
  <rect x="0.9" y="4.44" width="265.8" height="1.57" fill="#1d2420"/>
  <rect x="0.9" y="6.01" width="265.8" height="33.99" fill="#4a4a4d"/>
  <!-- the slot: black floor, 11.5 to 252.5 behind the bracket, 18.9 to 36.8 across -->

  <!-- nvidia/rtx-pro-4000-blackwell: THE SHROUD'S LOWER EDGE, the body's left
       side seen from outside. Across: 241.3 less mm behind the bracket's outer
       face, so the card's far end is at the left and the bracket's end at 240.4.
       Down: the face's y, the shroud's 6.01 to 20.48. A plain dark edge: no
       photograph shows it, and the broad side's photograph shows it flat. -->
  <rect x="0" y="6.01" width="240.4" height="14.47" fill="#242425"/>
</svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240.4mm" height="18.71mm" viewBox="0.9 1.77 240.4 18.71">
  <!-- nvidia/rtx-pro-4000-blackwell: THE TOP EDGE, the body's right side seen
       from outside. Across: mm behind the bracket's outer face (0.9 to 241.3, the
       shroud's length). Down: the face's y (1.77 the backplate's outer face, 4.44
       the board's outer face, 20.48 the shroud's). Every piece whose right side is
       the card's top edge `shows: [right]` and carries its patch of this. The
       band of cross slits along it, the model name at the bracket end and the
       reserved mark at the far end are read off PNY's 3/4 view from above and are
       estimated (provenance body-top-edge). The stereo and sync connectors the
       same view shows near the bracket are not drawn. -->
  <defs>
    <!-- one cross slit 0.6 along on a 1.6 pitch -->
    <pattern id="cross-slits" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse" x="62" y="8.0" width="1.6" height="10.5">
      <rect x="0" y="0" width="0.6" height="10.5" fill="#060607"/>

  <rect x="0.9" y="1.77" width="240.4" height="2.67" fill="#232325"/>
  <rect x="0.9" y="4.44" width="240.4" height="1.57" fill="#1d2420"/>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="79.2mm" height="41.91mm" viewBox="0 0 79.2 41.91">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="79.2mm" height="18.42mm" viewBox="0 0 79.2 18.42">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="120.02mm" height="41.91mm" viewBox="0 0 120.02 41.91">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>
